correctness.rationale: Centering the test vector with class levels (3/2,1/2,−1/2,−3/2) gives squared norm D/N; every spoke and the bridge have squared difference one, and every optional edge has zero. The Rayleigh bound is therefore BN/D. Equality requires full budget on the tree edges and the centered vector to be an eigenvector. Its peripheral equations fix the spokes individually; the hub equation fixes the bridge, so equality is rigid without assuming equal input weights or graph symmetries. At that candidate let λ=BN/D. The leaf-transverse eigenvalues are 3qB/D and 3pB/D, with multiplicities p−2 and q−2. In the strict balanced range both exceed λ. In the remaining four-dimensional quotient, eliminating the two positive leaf pivots of L−λI gives a two-by-two hub matrix with off-diagonal −b and a null vector with opposite signs. Both diagonal entries are negative, so exactly one quotient direction is negative and its only zero direction is the designated eigenvector. At q=2p the left pivot is positive and the right pivot is zero; after eliminating the left pivot, the reduced matrix has a hub coupled nontrivially to two zero-diagonal uncoupled coordinates, and inertia is one positive, one negative, one zero. The remaining transverse eigenvalues are nonnegative after the shift. Interchanging p,q handles the other endpoint. Outside the range the larger peripheral class has a positive-dimensional transverse block below λ, so the sole equality candidate fails and compactness makes the optimum strictly smaller. For p=2,q=3,B=1, independent exact calculation gives det(xI−34L)=x(x−5)(x−6)(x−18)(x−39), verifying simplicity and multiplicities. Wan et al.'s actual hypothesis of a non-repeated optimum is satisfied, and its designable edge set includes the zero-weight triangle edge, so the example contradicts the uniqueness-implies-tree direction as stated.
residual_risks: The claim is not an exact unbalanced-regime formula. ‘Sharp’ for BN/D means achieved in the balanced part of the family, not achieved for a fixed unbalanced pair.
The graph in the converse counterexample is the designable graph, not the support of the unique design; the hypothesis on simplicity is essential to quoting the theorem accurately.

evidence: Wan writes that, if at least one optimal design has non-repeated algebraic connectivity, the optimizer is unique ‘if and only if the designable edge set forms a tree’. The reported eigenvalues for p=2,q=3 verify that hypothesis and the allowed graph has a triangle.

The known tree Fiedler/test vector gives useful structure for the cyclic proof. Forcing every optional edge to zero and fixing all used weights require applying the Rayleigh equality conditions on the larger feasible set; the hypotheses and conclusion of the double-broom theorem itself concern only trees.

evidence: On a tree, Richter–Rocha normalize total weight to N−1. Scaling weights by B/(N−1) gives the budget-B objective; the budget inequality is saturated at any positive optimum.

At diameter d=3 the double broom is the spoke–bridge tree, and its parameter k is (|p−q|/2) for even N and (|p−q|−1)/2 for odd N. The transition in Theorem 1 is at k=N/6 for even N and k=N/6−1/2 for odd N, which translates to max(p,q)=2 min(p,q).
Wan distinguishes the allowed set E from its positive-weight support. Cyclic E with a tree support is not the tree-designable problem.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The tree normalization and size threshold are genuinely equivalent formulations of the known specialization. Adding optional edges changes the feasible set and is not a change of notation.

value.rationale: The counterexample addresses a published structural criterion, not a small numerical improvement. Its exact spectrum and Rayleigh rigidity distinguish a cyclic allowed graph with a unique optimizer from its tree support. The full family shows when a simple explicit certificate works and rules out attainment outside the size range, for any subset of internal peripheral edges. This value does not rest on recomputing the double-star tree optimum already available from the double-broom formula.
residual_risks: The architecture has one bridge and the only optional edges are within peripheral classes. It does not give a general replacement characterization for unique designs on arbitrary cyclic graphs.
